parsed.explanation: The combined regime places an adult trans visitor at high risk and a trans minor at severe risk. Assigned-sex passport and visa rules make border outing operationally likely; discrepancy can trigger refusal, additional evidence demands, fraud scrutiny, or detention. Federal facility exclusion and immigration/custody reports show birth-sex placement, forced labour, solitary confinement, sexual abuse, and care denial. The state’s lack of a local bathroom ban and city ordinances reduce ordinary private encounters but do not neutralise federal facilities or custody. Courts and hate-crime provisions exist, yet remedy is slow and uncertain.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports/visas tied to assigned sex; new X processing halted; entry cable demands evidence for mismatch; refused cases, additional checks, possible fraud/lifetime ineligibility; travellers report passports confiscated or blocked.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; foreign gender markers may pass where no doubt exists; pending civil-liberties suit and some injunctions; no binding visitor exemption documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Document or body mismatch at screening can escalate into refusal, travel advisory, immigration detention, and assigned-sex facility exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse; corrections bureau adopts assigned-sex policies, hair cuts, HRT removal, psychiatric substitution.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some orders are enjoined; national hate-crime and employment rulings exist but are not shown to control custody; legal FAQ exists without evidence of effective custody relief.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry scrutiny or facility complaint can move traveller into detention where assigned-sex placement and care denial are documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal single-sex government facilities exclude identity-based use; parent states have bathroom bans and a capitol trespass arrest; state facility bill passed one chamber but is not law.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state has no local bathroom ban and two city ordinances protect restroom use; a school injunction exists, but it does not override federal facility restrictions.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local ordinances may make ordinary private encounters safer, but federal buildings, detention, and custody remain exposed.

care_services.exposure: Trans minor cannot obtain gender-affirming care under state ban; national rules target youth care; custody care denial documented.
care_services.protection: Adult care availability is not documented; no visitor shield statute or documented emergency-care protection is shown.
care_services.interaction: A minor care-seeker may become investigated or outed; adult traveller may avoid care friction unless detained or in federal facility.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy frames radically pro-trans groups as hostile; executive orders deny identity language and target care; parent states criminalise bathroom use in some circumstances.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime aggravator for gender identity; employment-discrimination ruling; city employment ordinances; no enforcement data shown.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing increases severity of police, school, and facility interactions, making partial protections weaker.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors face state care denial, school name/pronoun notification, teacher criminalisation, and funding freezes; guardian may be drawn into outing or investigation.
minors_guardians.protection: City ordinances and school injunction protect some local settings; no documented guardian shield or rapid remedy.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family travel can combine school, medical, and screening encounters, producing document mismatch and state custody concerns.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific street-violence campaign documented for this state; parent capitol trespass arrest and federal facility enforcement create police exposure.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime enhancement for perceived gender identity; national hate-crime statute; city ordinances; no enforcement or visitor recourse documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response may enforce assigned-sex rules or lead to custody rather than provide protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Civil-liberties challenges pending; no visitor complaint office; facility and custody remedies absent; hate-crime enforcement unknown; adult care status uncertain.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Some orders are enjoined; local ordinances exist; legal-risk assessments and advisories signal scrutiny, but do not guarantee relief.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Timing of litigation may change exposure, but a passport, facility, or custody event can occur before relief is possible.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.25-D: it also has active entry-screening refusals, immigration custody sexual violence, and minor care denial. Local lack of bathroom ban offsets only private or state facilities, not federal exposure.
Safer than 0.15-D: no mandatory registration, checkpoint listing, or automatic fraud prosecutions. Shared custody harm and hostile state framing nevertheless keep it near the severe-risk edge.

Above 0.35-B: both have birth-sex placement exposure, but national entry rules, fraud scrutiny, custody abuse, and counterterrorism framing are more direct and visitor-facing than provincial service friction.

parsed.synthesis: Interaction drives the rating: passport or body mismatch at screening can become visa refusal, advisory, immigration detention, and assigned-sex facility placement. Once detained, documented sexual abuse, forced labour, solitary confinement, and care denial apply. Federal facility restrictions operate even though this state lacks a local bathroom ban and has city protections. Adult alone may pass if documents match presentation, but discovery consequences remain severe; trans minor lowers safety due care denial and school exposure. Partial legal protections leave a hostile combined operative regime unresolved.
